options.label: Same direction, very different length
options.content: Vector A points at (1, 1); vector B points at (10, 10) - ten times longer, but pointing exactly the same way. Cosine similarity: 1.0 (identical). This matches intuition for embeddings: a short sentence and a much longer passage expressing the same idea should be able to score as highly similar, and cosine similarity delivers that by ignoring how far out each vector reaches.

options.label: Similar length, different direction
options.content: Vector A points at (1, 1); vector C points at (1, -1) - nearly the same length, but at a right angle to A. Cosine similarity: 0.0 (unrelated). Raw distance between the two ENDPOINTS might look moderate here, but the angle - which is what cosine similarity actually measures - correctly flags these as pointing in unrelated directions, i.e. representing unrelated meaning.
